newsitem.title: USA: Dornan contests election in House of Representatives.
newsitem.headline: Dornan contests election in House of Representatives.

text.p: Republican Representative Robert Dornan, one of the most conservative members of Congress, filed papers Thursday seeking to overturn his November defeat by Democrat Loretta Sanchez, his attorney said.

Dornan, a feisty Republican known as "B-1 Bob" because of his strong support for the military, filed the complaint in Washington with the House of Representatives, according to his attorney Michael Schroeder.

Dornan, 63, asked the House to throw out the Nov. 5 election results and order a new election because of what he called voting irregularities, Schroeder said. He alleged about 3,500 ballots were illegally or improperly cast in November.
"We believe that a number of people worked together in concert to cause many of the improperly cast ballots in order to affect the outcome," Schroeder said.
The November results showed Dornan lost by 984 votes, but he and his supporters alleged non-citizens voted and that ballot boxes were not correctly sealed after the polls.

Earlier this month, a recount of ballots from the Nov. 5 election showed that Sanchez beat Dornan by 979 votes. Orange County election officials said the recount failed to uncover any major irregularities.
